summary:
• Chemical bonding is the force that holds atoms together in molecules. This force helps form different types of bonds between atoms.
• Bonds can be ionic or covalent and are formed when atoms share or exchange electrons. Ionic bonds happen when one atom loses an electron to become a positive ion (cation).
• Covalent bonds occur when two atoms share pairs of electrons. The Kössel-Lewis approach explains how chemical bonds form by looking at the electronic configuration of elements.

• Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons to achieve stability. The octet rule states that atoms want to have eight electrons in their outermost energy level.
• Lewis symbols show valence electrons and help calculate common or group valence. Examples include [Ne] 3s1 for sodium (one electron in the outer shell).
